Level 2 · Intermediate

Python Cheat Sheet

Level 2: keep this beside your keyboard

Print it (PDF, 36 KB) Dyslexia-friendly edition (PDF)

Types of values

7, -3 int: whole number
3.5, 0.1 float: decimal number
"7", "Nova" str: text (string)
True, False bool: yes or no 
n = int("7") * 2    # text -> int
label = str(42)     # int -> text
print(type(3.5))    # float

f-strings: build messages

hero = "Nova"
score = 12
print(f"{hero} has {score} points")
print(f"{score / 5:.1f}")  # 2.4

and, or, not

if score > 10 and lives > 0:
    print("Level up!")
if key == "q" or key == "Escape":
    running = False
if not game_over:
    move()

Functions: def and return

def area(width, height):
    """Area of a rectangle."""
    return width * height

big = area(3, 4) + 1   # 13

return hands a value back. print only shows it. Variables made inside a function stay inside (scope).

Lists

colors = ["orange", "sky", "green"]
first = colors[0]    # index from 0
last = colors[-1]    # the last one
colors.append("blue")  # add at end
print(len(colors))   # 4
for color in colors:
    print(color)
if "green" in colors:
    print("green is there")
pick = random.choice(colors)

while loops

lives = 3
while lives > 0:
    lives = lives - 1   # must change!

while True:          # ask again
    answer = input("How many? ")
    if answer.isdigit():  # a number?
        break        # leave the loop
    print("Try again")

Stuck in a loop that never ends? Press the red Stop button.

Nested loops (grids, pixel art)

for row in range(3):
    for col in range(4):
        print(row, col)

Dictionaries: look up by name

player = {"hero": "Nova", "score": 0}
player["score"] = player["score"] + 5
player["lives"] = 3         # new key
for key, value in player.items():
    print(key, value)
if "lives" in player:
    print(player["lives"])
speed = player.get("speed", 1)

Strings

line = "  12 apples \n"
clean = line.strip()   # "12 apples"
parts = clean.split()  # 2 words
print("Hi".upper(), "Hi".lower())

Files: save and load

with open("scores.txt", "w") as file:
    file.write("15\n")
with open("scores.txt", "a") as file:
    file.write("9\n")

try:
    with open("scores.txt") as file:
        scores = file.read().split()
except FileNotFoundError:
    scores = []      # no file yet

Careful: "w" empties the file first!

Testing with pytest

def test_area_normal():
    assert area(3, 4) == 12

def test_area_edge():     # edge case
    assert area(0, 4) == 0

Test names start with test_. To run them, open my_tests.py (or check_my_work.py) and press Run. No pytest? Tools > Manage packages.

Turtle events and games

screen = turtle.Screen()
screen.tracer(0)       # no flicker

def go_left():
    player.setx(player.xcor() - 20)

screen.onkey(go_left, "Left")  # no ()
screen.listen()        # hear keys

def game_loop():
    if player.distance(star) < 20:
        print("caught!")   # touching
    screen.update()
    screen.ontimer(game_loop, 50)

game_loop()
turtle.done()

Key names: "Left", "Right", "Up", "Down", "space", "a". Click the window first!

Error message decoder

Read the last line first. The line above it shows where.

SyntaxError typo: missing : ) or "
IndentationError spaces at the start of a line
NameError a name is misspelled or not made yet
TypeError mixing types: "5" + 5
IndexError no item at that index (too big)
KeyError that key is not in the dictionary
FileNotFoundError no file with that name in this folder
ValueError int("hello") cannot work

Debugging strategies

1. Read the traceback (last line first). 2. Print-debugging: print("x is", x) to see values. 3. Rubber duck: explain each line out loud.
